analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The patch excerpt shows a 'Last updated' date bump and a runtime-constants table edit. That edit documents a new CoordinatorReconnectPolicy: a stable-session backoff reset after 60s counted from the register frame, and a random 0..1s wait after close code 1012 with no backoff growth. The supplied units are base_text excerpts (lines 398-1305) of unchanged surrounding documentation. The changed lines at about 1937 are outside those excerpts, so I could not see the head text, and the patch excerpt is truncated. No code is changed in this batch.

Security relevance is limited to availability and reconnect behavior on TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket). Two points need checking in the actual source (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, which is not supplied): whether the 1012 fast-reconnect path of up to 1s with no growth could amplify load on the coordinator or bypass backoff if an adversarial or buggy peer repeatedly sends 1012, and whether the register-frame-based reset interacts with re-attestation or App Attest grant renewal in TB-011 (T-053, T-057). The coordinator is trusted, so this is a minor DoS or thundering-herd consideration rather than a regression, and it is not provable from documentation alone.

The base excerpts I examined (logout, drain, enroll, prefix-cache posture text) are pre-existing and unchanged. They show no new attack surface, and none of the retained threat entries, including T-041 and T-053, are contradicted by the doc edit. Remaining question: confirm the code behind the documented reconnect policy does not weaken connection-bound authorization, since each reconnect must obtain a fresh grant.
